epoch_ai.synthesis: The Epoch Brief (Sept 12) rounds up Huawei's chip roadmap lagging Nvidia, GPT-6 Astra's benchmark records, and a new math benchmark; separately, their Aug 27 data insight tracks how fast Anthropic and OpenAI are actually growing revenue — the empirical bull-case data point behind the capex buildout debate.

semianalysis.synthesis: This week's pieces are infrastructure-economics, not news: whether robotics inference belongs on-device or in a datacenter (a real cost/latency tradeoff, not hype), why 4-hi HBM memory packaging is winning out over higher-stack alternatives, and — most relevant to the market-risk thread — a piece on Nvidia's 'backstop' financing role across the AI buildout, framed as concentration risk (who actually eats the loss if a deal unwinds).

ed_zitron.synthesis: Zitron's latest pushes back hard on a former Anthropic researcher's public 'AI could recursively self-improve, I'm scared' narrative, arguing the coverage anthropomorphizes model risk while sidestepping concrete, already-documented harms — consistent with his standing bear-case framing that AI-safety alarm often substitutes for AI-labor/AI-finance accountability. Note: the RSS feed's description field is not usable for synthesis (confirmed unreliable) — this is from the live article directly.

farmdoc_daily.synthesis: The most substantive piece this week is a farmdoc analysis of the Gardner Food and Agricultural Policy Survey (Feb vs. Aug 2026 waves): public concern about AI/data-center development rose across every measured dimension in six months, with rural respondents consistently most concerned. Electricity costs remain the top worry (5.52/7 average, rural residents at 5.83/7), followed by water overuse (5.32/7) and agricultural land conversion (5.22/7) — all three crossed the 5.0 threshold for the first time this wave. Directly on-thesis for the farmland/AI-adjustment angle: this is public sentiment data, not just siting activity.

data_center_dynamics.synthesis: Nothing Indiana/Midwest-specific this week — this week's items are a rural Kansas 5G deal, a Brookfield real-estate minority stake, and a Turkish data center. Skipping rather than padding; DCD's feed stays broad industry news and needs this filter most weeks.

drought_monitor.synthesis: Indiana remains essentially drought-free as of the week of Sept 8 (96.2% no classification, 3.8% D0/abnormally dry, 0% D1+), up slightly from 0% D0 two weeks earlier — a small uptick worth watching but still far from the D2+ range that would matter for the farmland thesis. First week of history tracked in this pipeline, so no longer trend yet.

nass_crop_progress.synthesis: Indiana corn as of week ending Sept 6: 68% dented, 95% dough, 12% mature, harvest just starting (0% grain harvested, 30% silage harvested — silage comes off well before grain corn, so this isn't a discrepancy). Soybeans: 96% setting pods, 23% dropping leaves — both crops tracking a normal late-season pace, nothing anomalous.

interconnection_fyi.synthesis: No change since the pipeline's first snapshot (Sept 12): still 56 tracked Indiana data-center projects (33 proposed, 13 cancelled, 6 under construction, 4 operational), led by Lake and Porter counties. Nothing to report yet — two data points isn't enough to call a trend, but the cancelled-project count (13 of 56, nearly a quarter) is worth watching as the ledger accumulates more weeks.
